newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shares end up on chipmakers, Kim overlooked.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shares end up on chipmakers, Kim overlooked.

text.p: The Seoul composite stock index rebounded slightly in the late Tuesday afternoon session, boosted by buying in memory chip stocks, brokers said.
President Kim Young-sam's address to the nation, in which he apologised for the Hanbo Steel loan scandal, had no measurable affect on the market, they added.

The stock index rose 6.22 points to provisionally close at 682.81. Despite the climb, declining shares outpaced advancers 421 to 344. "The market jumped in the last 20 or 30 minutes of trading, mostly on institutional buying of large-cap shares," said Joo Sang-soo of Hanyang Securities.
Semiconductor shares rose on news that Merrill Lynch had recommended two U.S. memory chip stocks on good PC demand.
Samsung Electronics ended 3,200 won higher at 57,000, Hyundai Electronics rose 2,500 won to 34,100, and LG Semicon gained 1,700 won to 25,500.
Sentiment was also boosted by investors still hopeful that the foreign shareholding ceiling would be raised earlier than expected.
Despite official denial, talk circulated that the government would soon boost the foreign shareholding ceiling.

Local newspaper reports said the foreigner limits would be eased twice this year. South Korea has pledged to expand the ceiling to 23 percent from the current 20 percent, but a time schedule has not yet been announced.
"The market consensus is that it could happen as soon as April 1," said a UBS Securities broker.
During his televised address to the nation, Kim pledged to speed reform to eliminate corruption in the financial sector, but gave no details.
"The market did not take what Kim had to say very seriously," said a local trader.
"Tomorrow, the market could start on a rebound due to follow-through buying," said Hanyang Securities' Joo.
But he did not expect the market to be able to maintain an upward momentum due to continued poor fundamentals.

Brokers said that customer deposits at brokerages have begun to fall again. On Friday, the deposits were valued at 2.92 trillion won, down 1.56 percent from the previous day. Loans for margin trading, on the other hand, rose 1.21 percent to 2.85 trillion won.
The March futures contract closed 0.7 of a point higher at 69.15, while the KOSPI-200 index rose 0.76 of a point to 70.47.
